summary.tldr: Allows some survivors to receive federal pension benefits even if the marriage or common-law relationship started after age 60 or after retirement.
what_it_does: Allows survivors under several federal pension laws to receive benefits after the member dies, even if the marriage or conjugal relationship began after the person turned 60 or retired.
Repeals provisions in the Canadian Forces, judges, MPs, public service, and RCMP pension laws that reduced or blocked survivor benefit options in some cases.
Updates the definition of “survivor” for MPs’ pensions so it means a spouse immediately before death or a common-law partner who lived with the member for at least one year before death.
Changes child allowance rules in the Canadian Forces, Public Service, and RCMP pension laws, including higher amounts when there is no eligible survivor.
Updates federal pension plan rules so survivors can receive benefits from defined contribution accounts and joint-and-survivor pensions, and it revokes earlier elections to reduce some pensions.
summary.background: The bill amends several federal pension laws and pension plan rules about survivor benefits.
